newsitem.title: INDIA: India to deport criminal to France this week.
newsitem.headline: India to deport criminal to France this week.

text.p: Notorious criminal Charles Sobhraj will be deported from India to France this week, ending months of uncertainty over his future, his Indian lawyer said on Sunday.
Sobhraj, who has an Indian father and Vietnamese mother and claims French citizenship, served 20 years in an Indian jail on a string of charges including murder and robbery.
His lawyer Rajan Bakshi told Reuters his client would finally leave for France on Tuesday.
"He will be deported to France on an Air France flight, scheduled to leave at 0.30 a.m. (1900 GMT) on Tuesday morning," Bakshi said.
Bakshi said two officials of the Foreigners' Regional Registration Officer (FRRO) would accompany Sobhraj to France.
India ordered Sobhraj's deportation in February but France refused to accept him pending checks on his past record and nationality claim.
France agreed on Friday to supply Sobhraj with a travel document that would allow him to enter the country.
"Our embassy will in the next few days deliver to Charles Sobhraj a travel document giving him access to French territory," France's Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said on Friday.

"Competent authorities will continue to examine his situation. Given the elements at our disposal, we did not think we could oppose his coming to France," Doutriaux said, adding that Paris had not managed to establish his nationality.

Sobhraj, whose exploits across Asia have been the subject of two books, spent more than 20 years in a high-security Indian jail before being released on bail last month. He was immediately detained on the grounds that he lacked proper papers.

Sobhraj was first arrested in India for holding up a hotel jewellery shop in 1971. He was later charged with a long string of crimes including murder, serving time for some and winning acquittal in others.
Bakshi said the end to the Sobhraj stalemate was a result of the combined efforts of his lawyers in the Indian capital and French lawyer Jacques Verges in Paris.
"Mr. Verges helped expedite matters from Paris and we kept up the pressure from here," Bakshi said.
The controversial Verges is one of France's leading criminal lawyers who represented former Gestapo chief Klaus Barbie and international guerrilla Carlos the Jackal.
